plan.title: Paired 3-condition DE: treatment A/B vs control
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12 human blood samples: 4 subjects, each measured under control, treated_a, and treated_b (12000 genes x 13 columns in counts.csv, first column gene symbol; metadata.csv holds subject and condition). The question is which genes respond to either treatment within a subject and whether the two treatments differ from each other. Because each subject contributes one sample to every condition, the subject is a blocking factor that must precede condition in the design, removing between-subject variance and making every comparison within-subject. The plan follows the returned procedure: blind-vst sample-structure QC; a minimal low-count pre-filter; DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors with no pre-scaling; a DESeq2 LRT (~ subject + condition vs ~ subject) to find any gene that differs among the three conditions within subjects, followed by three named Wald contrasts (treated_a vs control, treated_b vs control, treated_b vs treated_a) with control as the explicitly set reference level; ashr shrinkage (the contrasts are not single coefficients, so apeglm does not apply); BH adjustment within each contrast at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering and a p-value histogram check; a limma-voom duplicateCorrelation pass as the independent second method for the robustness overlap; and a report carrying shrunken and unshrunken LFC, fit diagnostics, and the responder classification (A-only, B-only, shared, A-vs-B-different). Caveat stated up front: the input is already a gene-level integer count matrix summed from Salmon, and no transcript-level quant files exist in this analysis, so tximport length-scaled offsets (rule R-0018) cannot be applied; differential transcript usage is out of scope and the report will state this. With n=4 subjects per condition, power is limited and Cook's-distance outlier flagging will set some p-values to NA; flagged genes are reported, not silently dropped.
